## Body

Adds the launch-transition case to the existing related-row consumer-sufficiency note.

Spawn/revive starts the child before committing its fresh prebind. A new host querying related rows can therefore see the previous incarnation's tombstone under its reused durable seat id. An id-only terminal-close rule permanently stops a valid revive (R270-001).

Scope final closure to the requested launch: compare the row's spawn_id with PIJ_SPAWN_ID. Spawn and revive mint a fresh token; Copilot /restart inherits it. Without a spawn token, use the same native conversation OR the exact pid+proc_start as the legacy witness. An old tombstone with another launch token must retry until the fresh prebind appears; a genuinely closed same-launch restart must still stop. Existing open-row selection takes precedence.

Keep the two-snapshot regression, not just an absent-row prebind test: old closed same-id/old-launch -> retry -> open same-id/new-launch -> register. Preserve a same-conversation version too, so conversation equality cannot override a different launch token. Steady-live full-roster/related-row equivalence does not prove this transition.

Regression anchors: #270 at e385e0e2540962d9d6add6d92a061789adbfa1c6; .copilot/extensions/pij/store.mjs chooseRegistration; store.test.mjs and extension.test.mjs tests prefixed R270-001. Daemon ordering: crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs launch_seat_locked. The round-2 fix intentionally preserved launch-failure/postmortem ordering rather than redesigning spawn.
